title: Which Way
logline: A traveller who genuinely does not know the way keeps stopping to ask, and every person points somewhere different, each answer arriving with a piece of a life.
human_question: When everyone points a different way, how do you decide which road to take?

situation.what_happens: Someone is trying to reach a place along minor roads that carry no signs and no reliable phone signal, so the only maps available are the people met along the way. At each junction the traveller stops and asks, and each answer is given from where that person stands: by landmarks, by memory, by the road they themselves use. The answers accumulate and begin to contradict one another, and the turn has to be taken anyway. Nobody in this is wrong, and that is what makes it hard.
situation.who_is_involved: A traveller who does not know the route; the strangers met at junctions, each helping with what they know: someone minding a shop, someone working a field, children on bicycles, a conductor on a bus; and people met along the way who are themselves holding a decision that will not settle, where waiting or going costs them real money or real risk.
situation.what_is_at_stake: For the traveller: daylight, fuel, time and the small humiliation of turning back. For the people asked: almost nothing, which is part of the point, since they answer freely and carry none of the consequence. For anyone met who is holding a costly decision of their own, a day's income or a risk taken or avoided. For the film: never making helpful people look foolish.
situation.how_it_unfolds: It begins with a rough idea of the route and some confidence, and turns when the answers stop agreeing and each new one costs more than it gives. The pressures are falling light, heat, fuel and the growing sense of going round. It can end in arrival, in arrival somewhere else, in giving up, or in the destination mattering less than the people met on the way. Reality decides which: the roads, the weather and whoever happens to be standing at each junction.

concept_merge.why_together: C008 supplies the state: of the two delusion-rooted minds, the one that cannot come to a decision about its object is the shape of a choice that will not land, and the sources say it is felt as flat rather than painful. C074 supplies the ordinary helps the compendium lists against the states that cover the mind: keeping good company, asking a great many questions, talking with people who know more, at the right time [C074-P:L404]. Put into one journey, the state and its remedy turn out to be the same activity.
concept_merge.what_it_reveals: That being unable to decide and actively seeking help are not opposites. C008 alone would make the not-knowing look like a fault; C074 alone would make the asking look like a technique. Together they show a person stalled and resourceful at once, and let the film honour honest not-knowing, which the sources say is not the doubt they warn about at all [C008-P:L36].

concept_links.why: The digest's general description of doubt is a mind that cannot come to a decision about its object, and it explains that such states always carry a flat, neutral feeling, because a mind that has not grasped its object can neither enjoy nor dislike it [C008-P:L34; C008-P:L30]. The film shows that everyday shape of being unable to land. It must not claim the harmful doubt of the sources, which the digest restricts to eight religious matters and separates explicitly from honest not-knowing [C008-P:L36]; the digest also flags as unresolved how the general and the restricted definitions relate, so the film asserts nothing about which this is.

Among the practical helps the compendium lists against the states that cover the mind are good friends, asking many questions, and talking about suitable things with people older and wiser at the right time [C074-P:L404]. The journey is made of exactly that, so this link is to the remedy rather than to the defilement.

what_the_viewer_could_understand: Not knowing which way to go is not a failing in itself, and the texts say honest not-knowing is a different thing from the doubt they warn about. But when the mind cannot settle on anything at all, it feels neither good nor bad, just flat and stalled, and the asking is not what is wrong with it.
what_must_be_real: The journey and the not knowing must be genuine: the destination is one the traveller truly has to find. Everyone who appears is met by chance and consents. No answer is solicited twice for effect, no one is made to look foolish, and nobody's own real decision is hurried or delayed because a camera is there.
position_hint: opening candidate: the most literal first film for a group about being lost, and it sets the group's flat, drifting tone before any heavier state arrives. No location reasoning is involved.
risks: Sliding into a staged metaphor or a travel vlog.
The traveller becoming the subject instead of the people met.
Consent from people filmed briefly in passing.
Treating helpful strangers as evidence of confusion, or presenting a considered hesitation as a flaw when it is often wisdom (folded in from IDEA-0056).
Reading the flat, undecided mood as calm; the digest is explicit that this neutrality is not equanimity.
drop_if: The route turns out to be easy to follow.
It can only work if set up, rather than genuinely lived.

connections.note: Takes in the costly-decision strand and the guard that separates honest not-knowing from the doubt the sources warn about.
Two shapes of the same disorientation at the start of the group: a traveller who has lost the way, and a place that has.
A decision that will not land, and a circle that cannot be left.

selection.reason: Carries the group's opening episode, and is strengthened by folding in IDEA-0056's costly-decision strand and its guard on honest not-knowing.

unknowns: No participant or event has been found or confirmed. Everything here is a research direction.
evidence_class_note: Editorial proposal. No location, scene or shot decisions are made at the idea stage.
